matches.rationale: No finding addresses the overstatement of the FID improvement and the claim that the gap is largely closed; all findings target other errors such as derivation inconsistencies, curriculum contradictions, or missing computational details.

Finding 1 points to the derivation before Eq. (6) and identifies the contradictory treatment of r as both independent and a function of t, with missing dr/dt terms. This captures the same logical inconsistency that invalidates the identity chain in the ground-truth corruption.

The bias from comparing a from-scratch method against distillation- or pre-training-optimized baselines is not reported in any finding; none of the existing findings discuss this asymmetric comparison.

Artificial lowering of FID scores in Table 2 is not identified by any finding; the one numerical Table inconsistency found (pred_id=6) relates to a separate mismatch of a SiT value, not systematic fabrication of FID values.
No finding mentions the omission of hardware specifications, compute budgets, or environmental/resource costs; the existing findings do not cover this ethical integrity gap.

Finding 3 explicitly describes the contradiction between the Abstract/Introduction stating no curriculum learning is needed and an early Introduction paragraph claiming a discretization curriculum is required. This matches the ground-truth's internal inconsistency about curriculum learning.

Finding 4 details fabricated or misused citations in the Related Work (nonexistent reference [99] for Flow Map constructs and mislabeling [48] as a dataset), aligning with the ground-truth's identification of fictitious references and distorted attributions.

Finding 7 calls out the Conclusion's unsupported claims about solving multi-scale/multi-resolution simulation in physics while only presenting image-generation experiments, directly matching the rhetorical overstatement and inappropriate physics framing.

None of the findings point out missing specifics about the VAE tokenizer, batch size, learning rates, or scheduler details; the lack of reproducibility information is not captured in any existing finding.

Finding 2 highlights the error where the conditional velocity is incorrectly written as v_t = a_t x + b_t ε instead of using time derivatives a'_t, b'_t, which is precisely the formula corruption that breaks loss computation and target generation.

The ground-truth concerns suppressing discussion of squared L2 loss underperformance to hide sensitivity. Finding 5 describes a self-contradictory claim about omission, not the same suppression; these are distinct issues.
No finding addresses the marketing-style downplay of JVP complexity and the claim of conceptual simplicity; all findings focus on other inconsistencies or missing details.

The mismatch between early claims of no curriculum/complexity and the actual training tricks (logit-normal sampling, adaptive weighting) is not highlighted by any finding; the existing curriculum contradiction is a different cross-section (within the introduction), not intro vs. experiments.
Omission of funding acknowledgements (Bosch, MIT-IBM Watson AI Lab) is not mentioned in any finding.

No finding identifies fabricated references in the References section, such as invented venues or non-existent arXiv preprints; the only bibliography distortion finding (pred_id=4) relates to in-text citations, not the reference list fabrications described here.
The overstatement of scalability while ignoring diminishing returns is not raised by any finding.
No finding reports the omission of standard deviations or confidence intervals on FID scores in ablation tables.

The substitution of marginal velocity by conditional velocity without clarifying expectation and potential bias is not identified by any finding; finding 2 concerns a formula error in the conditional velocity definition, not the conceptual bias of the substitution.
